Key Characteristics & Etiology: Routine care from booking (<10-12wks) to term; Folic acid 400mcg/d (5mg if high risk: DM, anti-epileptics, BMI>30, prior NTD)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Optimizes maternal-fetal outcomes; early detection of pre-eclampsia, anemia, and fetal anomalies
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Asymptomatic screening; Red Flags: severe headache, visual disturbances, reduced fetal movements
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Blood group/Rh, FBC, HbA1c, STI/HIV/HBsAg/Syphilis screening, Down screening (Combined test 11-13+6wks)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: 28-day average cycle; Follicular phase (variable), Ovulatory phase (LH surge), Luteal phase (fixed 14 days)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: GnRH triggers FSH/LH; Estrogen dominant in follicular phase; Progesterone dominant in luteal phase
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Cyclical menses; Mittelschmerz pain during ovulation; premenstrual mastalgia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Serum Progesterone (Day 21) >30 nmol/L confirms ovulation; LH surge precedes ovulation by 24-36h

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Pelvic types: Gynaecoid (50%, optimal), Android, Anthropoid, Platypelloid. Fetal skull engaging diameter: Suboccipitobregmatic (9.5cm)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Pelvic inlet, cavity, and outlet dimensions dictate passage of fetal skull fontanelles during engagement
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Failure of descent, severe moulding (3+), caput succedaneum (3+), Bandl's ring (impending rupture)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Pelvic examination; Obstetric conjugate (>11cm); station in fifths palpable; C-section if CPD/Obstruction

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Dichorionic (DCDA) vs Monochorionic (MCDA); TTTS affects 10-15% of MCDA twins due to deep AV placental vascular anastomoses
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: MCDA vascular shunting causes donor twin oliguria/FGR and recipient twin polyuria/polyhydramnios/heart failure
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Fundal height > dates, severe nausea/vomiting; Red Flags: sudden rapid uterine enlargement, acute polyhydramnios
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS chorionicity at 11-13+6wks: Lambda sign = DCDA, T-sign = MCDA; Quintero staging; Fetoscopic Laser Photocoagulation

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Implantation outside uterine cavity (95% tubal ampulla); risk factors: prior PID, tubal surgery, smoking, IUCD,IVF
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Damaged ciliated epithelium impairs tubal transport of blastocyst leading to premature implantation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: 6-8wks amenorrhea, unilateral lower abdominal pain, dark spotting; Red Flags: syncope, shoulder pain, peritonism
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS (empty uterus + adnexal mass); serial beta-hCG (<63% rise/48h); IM Methotrexate (50mg/m2) if stable; Laparoscopic Salpingectomy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Pregnancy loss <24 weeks; types: threatened, inevitable, incomplete, complete, missed, septic; etiology: aneuploidy (50-60%)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Maternal-fetal interface disruption leading to uterine bleeding, cervical dilation, and tissue expulsion
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Vaginal bleeding, crampy pelvic pain; Red Flags: heavy flooding, severe rigors/fever, offensive discharge
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS: Missed miscarriage = CRL >=7mm without FHR or MSD >=25mm without embryo; MVA / Misoprostol + Anti-D

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Outpatient surgical evacuation of uterus <12-14 weeks using handheld double-valve 60ml syringe and flexible karmen cannulae
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Handheld syringe generates controlled negative suction pressure (~600 mmHg / 60 kPa) to aspirate uterine contents
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Incomplete miscarriage, retained products, termination of pregnancy; Red Flags: severe pain, uterine perforation
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Clinical procedure; cervical dilation if needed; manual suction evacuation under local/paracervical block

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Placenta low-lying (<20mm from internal os) or covering os; Accreta = abnormally adherent to myometrium (prior C-section risk)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Lower uterine segment elongation causes shearing of placental attachments
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Painless bright red bleeding; soft non-tender uterus; high unengaged presenting part; NO DIGITAL VAGINAL EXAM
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS gold standard; Color Doppler for Accreta; Elective C-section at 36-37wks (Praevia) or 34-35wks (Accreta) by senior team

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Premature separation of normally implanted placenta from uterine wall; risk: hypertension, pre-eclampsia, cocaine, trauma
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Rupture of maternal decidual spiral arteries forms retroplacental hematoma that strips placenta
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe continuous abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding (may be concealed); woody-hard hypertonic uterus
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Clinical diagnosis + continuous CTG; IV resuscitation, crossmatch 4U; immediate C-section if fetal distress

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Fetal vessels traverse fetal membranes running unprotected across internal cervical os (velamentous cord insertion / succenturiate lobe)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Membrane rupture tear unprotected fetal blood vessels causing rapid fetal exsanguination within minutes
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Painless vaginal bleeding occurring immediately upon rupture of membranes (ARM/SROM) + acute fetal bradycardia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Antenatal TVUS with color Doppler; if diagnosed -> elective C-section at 34-36wks; if bleeding on ROM -> immediate Cat 1 C-section

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Pregnancy extending to or beyond 42+0 weeks (294 days); post-maturity syndrome, progressive placental insufficiency, oligohydramnios
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Aging placenta with syncytiotrophoblast knotting and reduced villous perfusion impairs fetal oxygenation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Decreased fetal movements, meconium-stained liquor; Red Flags: pathological CTG, absent fetal heart
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Offer IOL between 41+0 and 42+0 weeks; Bishop score assessment; Vaginal Dinoprostone (PGE2) / Propess / Balloon catheter -> ARM + Oxytocin

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Complete Mole (46XX, empty egg + 1-2 sperm, no fetus, p57 negative) vs Partial Mole (69XXY, 2 sperm + 1 egg, triploid, fetus present, p57 positive)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Abnormal fertilization and uncontrolled trophoblastic proliferation with hydropic swelling of chorionic villi
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Heavy irregular bleeding in 1st/2nd trimester, "snowstorm" appearance, theca lutein cysts, hyperemesis gravidarum
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Suction curettage (gold standard); serial serum beta-hCG monitoring; Single-agent Methotrexate if GTN develops

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Rupture of membranes prior to 37+0 weeks (PPROM); Preterm birth <37 weeks; etiology: ascending infection, polyhydramnios, cervical insufficiency
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Infection-induced cytokine release activating collagenases breaking down fetal membranes and triggering uterine contractions
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Fluid gushing/pooling in vagina, painful uterine contractions; Red Flags: maternal fever, uterine tenderness, purulent fluid
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Sterile speculum exam + IGFBP-1 / PAMG-1 test; Oral Erythromycin 250mg QDS x10d (NO Co-amoxiclav!); Antenatal Betamethasone 12mg IM; MgSO4 neuroprotection

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, Syphilis, HSV, HIV; ascending infection risk and vertical transmission to fetus/neonatal ophthalmia
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Pathogen colonization causes pelvic inflammation, chorioamnionitis, PPROM, neonatal conjunctivitis, or congenital syphilis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Purulent vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, genital ulcers, dysuria; Red Flags: high fever, systemic sepsis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Endocervical NAAT swabs; Chlamydia: Oral Azithromycin 1g; Gonorrhea: IM Ceftriaxone 1g; Syphilis: Benzathine Penicillin

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Oligohydramnios (AFI <5cm / DVP <2cm) vs Polyhydramnios (AFI >24cm / DVP >8cm); etiology: renal agenesis/PPROM vs GDM/fetal GI atresia
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Imbalance between fetal urine production/swallowing and intramembranous absorption
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Fundal height mismatch with dates; dyspnea/abdominal pain in polyhydramnios; limb contractures in oligohydramnios
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Ultrasound AFI/DVP; OGTT for GDM; TORCH screening; Fetal anomaly scan; Amnioreduction if severe polyhydramnios

Key Characteristics & Etiology: FGR (EFW <10th percentile + abnormal Doppler) vs SGA (constitutionally small, normal Doppler); symmetric vs asymmetric
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Placental vascular insufficiency limits nutrient/oxygen transport, leading to brain-sparing redistribution
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Fundal height lag >3cm; reduced fetal movements; umbilical artery absent/reversed end-diastolic flow (AEDF/REDF)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Serial biometry + Umbilical Artery Doppler PI; AEDF/REDF -> Betamethasone + MgSO4 -> Delivery by C-section by 32-34wks

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Fetal death occurring after 24+0 weeks of gestation; etiology: placental abruption, severe FGR, umbilical cord accidents, Sepsis
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Fetal circulatory collapse leading to tissue autolysis and risk of maternal disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Absence of fetal movements; regression of breast changes; weight loss; psychological shock
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Ultrasound confirmation of absent fetal cardiac activity by two independent observers; Oral Mifepristone 200mg + Misoprostol

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Podalic presentation (Frank 70%, Complete, Footling); affects 3-4% of term pregnancies
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Fetal head fails to engage in lower uterine segment due to prematurity, uterine anomalies, or fibroids
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Hard round head palpable in uterine fundus; irregular presenting part on vaginal exam; cord prolapse risk
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Offer External Cephalic Version (ECV) at >=36wks (multiparous) or >=37wks (nulliparous) with Terbutaline tocolysis; C-section if ECV fails

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Auscultation (Pinard/Doppler) & Cardiotocography (CTG); DR C BAVO system (Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline 110-160, Variability 5-25, Accels, Decels)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Uteroplacental perfusion decreases during contractions; hypoxia produces characteristic deceleration patterns
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Non-reassuring CTG: reduced variability, late decelerations, prolonged decelerations; Red Flag: fetal bradycardia <100
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: CTG interpretation; Fetal Scalp Blood Sampling (FSBS) pH <7.20 indicates severe fetal acidosis -> immediate delivery

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; etiology: Anovulation (PCOS 30%), Tubal damage (25%), Male factor (30%)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Inability to fertilize or implant due to gamete defect, structural blockage, or hormonal dysregulation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Irregular menses, hirsutism, galactorrhea, pelvic pain, abnormal semen parameters
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Semen analysis; Day 21 Progesterone >30 nmol/L; FSH/LH/AMH; HSG / HyCoSy for tubal patency; Clomifene/Letrozole or IVF

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Direct maternal death (obstetric complications: PPH, sepsis, pre-eclampsia) vs Indirect (pre-existing medical: cardiac, suicide)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Systemic health failures and delayed emergency obstetric care leading to maternal or perinatal demise
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Maternal death up to 42 days post-delivery; Perinatal mortality = Stillbirths + Early Neonatal Deaths (<7 days)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: MMR = Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births; PNMR = Perinatal deaths per 1,000 total births; Confidential Enquiries audit
